name: Bhu Varaha Swamy Temple
deity: Varaha as Bhu Varaha Swamy, with Ambujavalli Thayar
significance: A Vishnu temple at Srimushnam dedicated to the boar avatar Varaha, whose earliest endowments date to the medieval Cholas. Its present form owes most to the Thanjavur Nayak ruler Achuthappa Nayak, with the rajagopura added under the Vijayanagara Empire.
story: Varaha is said to have taken boar form here to lift the earth goddess Bhudevi away from the asura Hiranyaksha, and the temple tank is held to have formed where his sweat fell.

name: Markandeshwar Temple
deity: Shiva as Markandeshwar
significance: A Shiva temple standing on the bank of the Markandeshwar tank north of the Jagannath temple at Puri. Both shrine and tank are dated to the 12th century and the tank counts among the sacred water bodies of the Puri pilgrimage.
story: The sage Markandeya is said to have meditated on Shiva here, and to have seen an infant afloat on a banyan leaf upon the waters, a vision Vishnu explained to him.

name: Ambika Jain Temple, Girnar
deity: Ambika, the Jain yakshi
builtDisplay: present shrine 15th c.; earliest temple 8th c.
significance: A hilltop shrine to the yakshi Ambika on Girnar, its earliest temple traced to the middle of the 8th century and the standing building to the 15th, after patronage by Vastupala and Tejapala and a rebuilding funded by the merchant Samal Sah in 1468. It draws Hindu as well as Jain pilgrims.
story: Newly married couples visit to tie their garments together and make offerings, in the belief that the goddess will grant them a long and happy marriage.

name: Karikkakom Devi Temple
deity: Chamundi Devi, worshipped as Maha, Raktha and Bala Chamundi
significance: A Chamundi temple on the western edge of Thiruvananthapuram, reckoned more than six centuries old, where the goddess is served in three distinct forms in separate sanctums.
story: Under the Travancore Maharajas the accused were brought before the sanctum of Raktha Chamundeswari to swear their innocence, in the belief that the goddess protects the truthful and punishes the liar.

name: Gurdwara Baba Atal
deity: Guru Granth Sahib, at the shrine of Baba Atal Rai
significance: A nine-storey octagonal tower some 40 metres high, raised over the samadhi of Baba Atal Rai, son of Guru Hargobind, just south of the Golden Temple. Its lower storeys were directed by Jodh Singh Ramgarhia and the rest funded by sardars and public donation, with the gilt dome given by Desa Singh Majithia.
story: Atal Rai is said to have restored his snake-bitten friend Mohan to life, and when his father rebuked the display of a miracle he withdrew and gave up his own life in 1628.

name: Gurdwara Mehdiana Sahib
deity: Guru Gobind Singh, commemorated at his resting place
significance: A gurdwara at Mehdiana marking where Guru Gobind Singh and his followers rested after the battle of Chamkaur in 1705 and where he set about composing the Zafarnamah. Begun under Jathedar Jora Singh Lakha around 1970, the complex has since grown to some 25 acres.
story: Sikhs hold that the place carries Guru Gobind Singh's blessing, and that prayers made on a visit here do not go unanswered.

name: Sathyagirisvarar Temple, Thirumayam
deity: Shiva as Sathyagirisvarar, with the goddess Venuvanesvari
significance: A rock-cut Shiva temple carved into the hill of Thirumayam Fort and attributed to the Pallavas. It stands beside a Vishnu temple, the pair long cited as an emblem of sectarian accord.

name: Gurudwara Guru Nanak Dham
deity: Guru Nanak, commemorated at the site of his visit
significance: A gurdwara on the island of Rameswaram built to mark the visit of Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, to the town in about 1511.

name: Parthasarathy Temple, Parthivapuram
deity: Vishnu as Parthasarathy, named Vishnu-bhattarakar in the inscriptions
significance: A Vishnu temple founded in 869 CE by the Ay king Karunandadakkan, its three-storeyed vimana fronted by a Garuda namaskara mandapa. Its copper plates record the endowment of an attached Vedic school for 95 students, making it a key document of early south Indian temple learning.

name: Raghunatha Temple, Alangiri
deity: Raghunath
significance: A nine-pinnacled nabaratna temple of 1810 raised by the Das family within the walled courtyard of their residence at Alangiri near Egra. Standing about forty feet high with triple-arched verandahs on three sides, it is among the largest temples of the Midnapore country.

name: Chowdeshwari Temple, Dasarighatta
deity: Chowdeshwari Devi, as Sri Ramalinga Chowdeswari Ammanavaru
significance: A goddess temple at Dasarighatta about ten kilometres from Tiptur, drawing pilgrims for its Tuesday worship and for Navaratri.

name: Narasimha Temple, Puri
deity: Narasimha, in his Shanta and Ugra forms
significance: A west-facing Narasimha temple about sixty feet high standing between the Gundicha temple and the Indradyumna tank at Puri, laid out on Vaishnava Agama principles and housing both the calm and the wrathful images of the deity.
story: The Skanda Purana tells that king Indradyumna had a Narasimha image carved in black stone and worshipped it here while preparing his Ashwamedha sacrifice, whence the deity is called Yajna Narasimha.

name: Gurdwara Nanaklama
deity: Guru Nanak, commemorated at the site of his third udasi visit
significance: A gurdwara at Chungthang in north Sikkim raised in 1969 by the Assam Rifles under Subedar Major Bhullar, helped by the local MLA Tasa Tangey Lepcha, in remembrance of Guru Nanak's visit during his third udasi.

name: Sri Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Manyamkonda
deity: Venkateswara as Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Swamy
significance: A hill shrine to Venkateswara about five kilometres from Devarakadra in Mahabubnagar district, and the first temple in Telangana to be given ropeway access.

name: Guru Ka Tal
deity: Guru Tegh Bahadur, to whose memory the shrine is dedicated
significance: A gurdwara at Agra dedicated to the memory of the ninth Guru, Tegh Bahadur, built in the 1970s through the efforts of Sant Baba Sadhu Singh Mauni beside a red sandstone reservoir of 1610 raised in Jahangir's reign for water conservation. Eight of the tank's original twelve towers survive, their carving akin to Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.
story: Sikh tradition holds that it was here that Guru Tegh Bahadur laid down his arms and offered himself for arrest before his martyrdom.

name: Keshabeshwar Temple
deity: Shiva, worshipped as a lingam
significance: A Shiva temple at Ramnathpur founded in 1748 by the zamindar Keshab Roychowdhury, whose architect Basudeb took twelve years over it. Its atchala roof carries a kalash and trishul, corridors run along three sides of the sanctum, and the Charak Puja fair is still held in its grounds.

name: Gurdwara Dam Dama Sahib
deity: Guru Gobind Singh, commemorated at the site of his 1707 meeting
significance: A Delhi gurdwara marking the meeting of Guru Gobind Singh with Prince Muazzam, later Emperor Bahadur Shah, in 1707. A bungalow of 1664 on the spot was rebuilt as a gurdwara by Sardar Baghel Singh in 1783 and later renovated under Maharaja Ranjit Singh, though most of the standing structure dates from after 1947.

name: Chehni Kothi
deity: Bhagwati
significance: A tall timber-and-stone tower at Chehni in the Banjar valley, about 350 years old and known as the Bhagwati temple for the goddess shrine it holds. It belongs to the wider Himachali tradition of village goddess cults and is celebrated for having withstood Himalayan earthquakes.
story: Local lore holds that the tower was the fortified seat of a ruler remembered as Queen Chaini, from whom the village takes its name.

name: Ladnu Jain temple
deity: Shantinatha, the 16th Tirthankara
significance: A Jain temple complex at Ladnu of five Digambara and two Shvetambara shrines, its principal Shantinatha temple carrying an inscription of 1295 CE. The town has been a Jain centre since the 10th century, is the birthplace of Acharya Tulsi and hosts Jain Vishva Bharati University.

name: Annapurna Temple, Titagarh
deity: Annapurna, with Shiva
significance: A nine-pinnacled navaratna temple opened on 12 April 1875 by Jagadamba Devi, youngest daughter of Rani Rashmoni, on the model of the Bhavatarini temple at Dakshineswar. Ramakrishna opened it to devotees; the Shiva image is silver and the Annapurna image of ashtadhatu, and the courtyard holds a natmandir, six Shiva shrines and two nahabatkhanas.

name: Muktidham
deity: Krishna, alongside replicas of the twelve Jyotirlingas
significance: A marble temple complex in the Nashik Road suburb, founded in 1971 on a donation from the industrialist J. D. Chauhan-Bytco. Rajasthani sculptors built it from Makrana marble, and it holds replicas of the twelve Jyotirlingas along with paintings by Raghubir Mulgaonkar.

name: Subai Jain temples
deity: Rishabhanatha, with Mahavira and Parshvanatha
builtDisplay: 4th c. by the site record; others date it before 750 CE
significance: A group of six Jain temples at Subai in Koraput district, ascribed to Jain gemstone traders of the region and described by the state as a medieval Jain monastic site. A four-foot Jain image was recovered here in a 2020 excavation, and the annual Parab festival is still kept at the site.

name: Gurdwara Patalpuri Sahib
deity: Memorial to Guru Hargobind, Guru Har Rai and Guru Har Krishan
significance: A gurdwara on the left bank of the Sutlej at Kiratpur where Guru Hargobind and Guru Har Rai were cremated and the ashes of Guru Har Krishan immersed. It remains the foremost place at which Sikhs consign ashes as part of the Antam Sanskar rites.
story: It is told that a Rajput raja and his followers threw themselves into Guru Hargobind's funeral pyre.

name: Nilamadhav Temple
deity: Vishnu as Nilamadhava
significance: A hill temple to Vishnu as Nilamadhava above Kantilo, near the meeting of the Mahanadi, Kuanria and Kusumi that Odias call their triveni sangam. Its structure follows that of the Jagannath temple at Puri.
story: The shrine is said to have begun when the Sabara chief Biswabasu worshipped the deity, known in his tongue as Kitung, as a blue sapphire image in a cave of the Brahmadri hills, before a wooden form took its place.

name: Kochi Jain temple
deity: Dharmanatha, the 15th Tirthankara
significance: A Shvetambara Murtipujak temple at Mattancherry built in 1904 by Hirubai Jivraj Dhanji in memory of her husband and run by the Cochin Swetamber Murtipujak Jain Sangh. Its white marble and sculptured pillars follow the Jain temples of Gujarat, the homeland of Kochi's Jain merchant community, and a second shrine holds Chandraprabha.

name: Gurdwara Baba Gurditta
place: Chandpur Rurki, Kiratpur Sahib, Rupnagar district
deity: Baba Gurditta, commemorated at his cremation place
significance: A gurdwara near Kiratpur marking where Baba Gurditta, son of Guru Hargobind and father of Guru Har Rai, died and was cremated on 15 March 1638. It is also kept in memory of Baba Kesra Singh.
story: Tradition holds that Gurditta reluctantly brought back to life a cow he had killed while hunting, and that rebuked by his father for working a miracle he withdrew from Kiratpur and died the same day, a neem tree at the spot springing from the twig in his hand.
